defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: Default devnull BufferedWriter matches neither TextIO nor int, so it is never closed in stop()
DEVNULL guard removed; os.close(DEVNULL) closes subprocess's shared fd
Binary streams admitted by IO[Any] are not closed by stop()
No guard against double stop(); second call raises ValueError/OSError
No test covers default None log_output path
No test covers DEVNULL as log_output
No test covers string path log_output
votes.evidence_quote: Default `open(os.devnull, "wb")` produces a `BufferedWriter` that matches neither `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` nor `isinstance(self.log_output, int)`, so `Service("chromedriver").stop()` never closes the devnull handle.
votes.justification: The review sees that the `TextIO` isinstance check misses the default devnull `BufferedWriter` and binary streams, so those leak. But it assumes real text files do match `TextIO` (it even claims a closed text file is "still True"), so it misses the root cause: `typing.TextIO` matches no real file object, and every file log stays open.
